newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares slip on slow interest in late trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares slip on slow interest in late trade.

text.p: German shares slipped in late dealings on Tuesday marked by profit-taking and a lack of institutional investor interest, eroding early gains tied to overnight Wall Street gains, traders said.
The DAX index was down 19.17 points at 3,573.97 points in post-bourse IBIS dealings and also lower than the DAX bourse index close, which ended up 19.78 points at 3,595.15 points.

"If there was major investor interest in the market, the trading volumes would surely have to be higher than what we see right now," said one Frankfurt trader. "We been at some lofty levels lately and it was time for some profit-taking."
Dealers said they expected the market to stay lower in the near-term despite the steady dollar and German debt market but would watch for U.S. market developments for influence.
The market earlier on Tuesday see-sawed, first stuttering after the U.S. surge, then regaining poise to send the blue chip DAX index to its second consecutive record closing high.
"Absolutely everything is working for us now," said a Frankfurt trader. "The dollar's not a big problem, company earnings are strong and rates don't look like rising."
But others said volumes were modest apart from selected stocks, and bemoaned relatively low activity from investors.

One of the pressures on trade was a slide by Deutsche Telekom AG, partly correcting a recent surge, after the telecommunications giant released 1996 data which partly exceeded bullish forecasts, but did not surprise, dealers said.
Telekom posted a net profit of 1.8 billion marks for the year, but eased 1.06 marks to 40.13 marks after notching up gains of as much as five percent at its height on Monday.

Deutsche Bank AG, which closed up 2.20 marks at 97.30 marks, was also a top focus as it traded just off an all-time high of 97.75 marks. Dealers tied the gains to technical factors, partly connected to an options expiry on Friday.
